section_sampled_diagnostic.method: inward rays from every vertex (stride shown) of the finished mesh off a crease (incident faces within 35 deg) to the first surface; spur points (radius under 0.4 mm) are reported apart
section_sampled_diagnostic.reading: Diagnostic only; the gate is the field's thinnest wall for the band and the sections by construction for every part. A single inward ray reads relief as section. The blossom clusters, opposite-wall ones included, come from rays leaving a petal's rolled rim sideways at the notch roots, where two petals' rims meet in a V and the ray crosses the V rather than the petal; a lone blossom with no band gives the same readings (least 0.16 mm at 2.4 to 2.7 mm across, 0.36 to 0.44 at 3.6 to 3.9), while every petal is 0.84 mm through its rim. On the wood the rays cross a fissure wall or a spur root at a slant.
